_comment: Default values for dashboard preferences that are persisted per-browser in localStorage. Read at init by the dashboard via GET /api/ui-defaults; used ONLY when the corresponding localStorage key is absent (first visit or after Settings → Clear Local Storage & Cookies). User toggles in the Settings popover always override and persist locally. Change a value here to shift the default for first-time visitors across all browsers served by this install. EXCEPTIONS: every key below that has its own _comment is not a localStorage-backed preference but a setting `npm run build` bakes into the dashboard bundle — see each comment. Because the bundle is built from this shipped file, an override of one of them in app-config/user-configurable/ has no effect; change it here and run `npm run build`.
_reloadMaxWaitMs_comment: How long, in milliseconds, the Reload Current Position dialog waits for its scan to finish before reloading the page anyway (14400000 = four hours). The dialogs quote this same figure as the longest a reload may take. Read by public/dashboard-reload-flow.js.
_pollFailuresBeforeHalted_comment: How many GET /api/status polls in a row may fail before the status pill reads HALTED. A single failed poll is usually a blip, so the pill waits for the server to have missed this many. Read by public/dashboard-data-poll.js.
_pollSkipLogEvery_comment: A poll is skipped while the previous GET /api/status request is still waiting for its answer. The browser console logs the first skip in a run and then one line in every this many, so a slow server does not flood the console. Read by public/dashboard-data-poll.js.
_lastCheckJustNowSec_comment: Mission Control's last-check tag reads "just now" for this many seconds after the bot's last look at the pool, and counts seconds after that. Read by public/dashboard-data-status.js.
_autoCompoundSyncHoldMs_comment: After Stop Managing is clicked, how long, in milliseconds, the dashboard leaves the Auto-Compound toggle alone instead of syncing it from status polls, so a poll answered before the server took in the stop cannot switch the toggle back on. Read by public/dashboard-data-status.js.
_throttleNearLimitPct_comment: The rebalance-throttle badge reads NEAR LIMIT once a pool has used this percentage of its Max Rebalances / Day, while nothing is blocking a rebalance yet. The badge's help text quotes the same figure. Read by public/dashboard-throttle.js and public/param-help-content.js.
_activityLogMaxEntries_comment: How many entries the Activity Log keeps; the oldest are dropped past this. Read by public/dashboard-helpers.js.
_copyFeedbackMs_comment: How long, in milliseconds, a copy icon or copy button shows that it copied, before returning to its usual look. Read by public/dashboard-helpers.js and public/dashboard-wallet.js.
_heapLogIntervalMs_comment: How often, in milliseconds, the dashboard logs its JavaScript heap size to the browser console (600000 = ten minutes). The dashboard is meant to stay open for days, so a figure that keeps rising across hours points at a leak. Chrome only. Read by public/dashboard-init.js.
_chainQueryTimeoutMs_comment: How long, in milliseconds, the dashboard gives the server to say which blockchain it runs (GET /api/chain). The dashboard asks at startup and builds no position key or url until it has the answer. A request that gets no answer within this time, or that ends without naming a blockchain, is logged to the browser console with what happened, and the dashboard asks again; it asks at most once per this interval, so a server that refuses at once is not asked in a tight loop. Unlike the preferences above, this is not read via /api/ui-defaults: it bounds the dashboard's first request, so it is needed before the server has answered anything. public/dashboard-chain.js therefore imports it from this file, and `npm run build` bakes it into the bundle. An override in app-config/user-configurable/ has no effect on it.
_dashboardPollIntervalMs_comment: How often, in milliseconds, the dashboard asks GET /api/status for fresh figures. The Reload Current Position dialog checks on its scan at the same pace, and the server uses this value to judge when the dashboard has had time to poll. Like chainQueryTimeoutMs, it is not read via /api/ui-defaults: the dashboard needs it before its first poll, so public/dashboard-data-poll.js imports it from this file and `npm run build` bakes it into the bundle. The server reads this shipped file too (src/config.js), so the two always agree, and an override in app-config/user-configurable/ has no effect on it.
_dialogMaxHeightPx_comment: Maximum height, in pixels, of EVERY dialog in the dashboard — both dialog families (.modal in style.css and .9mm-pos-mgr-modal in 9mm-pos-mgr.css, plus all their variants) and the IL/G debug popover. Past this height a dialog scrolls instead of growing until its dismiss button is pushed off-screen. Dialogs that carry a .9mm-pos-mgr-modal-body scroll just that body, so the title and the Close button stay pinned; the rest scroll as a whole, which is why the box also sets overflow-y. DELIBERATELY EXEMPT: the Disclosure (.disclaimer-box) — the user must scroll through the whole text to reach its accept/decline buttons, so bounding it would defeat its purpose. Anchored dropdown menus (Settings gear, ? Help, hover info popovers) are not dialogs and are not covered. Unlike the keys above, this is NOT persisted per-browser and is not read via /api/ui-defaults: `npm run build` bakes it into the generated public/ui-tokens.css as the --dialog-max-h custom property, so it applies on first paint with no inline styles and no runtime fetch. Per feedback_one_literal_per_shipped_default the literal lives here only — the CSS references the variable with no fallback value, so if the generated file is missing the dialogs simply revert to growing and the overlay scrolls.
